title: Propagate tier context (hosted/dedicated) through gateway → routing → runtime metrics
author: Caleb Johnson
description:
Context
We’re standardizing tiered SLIs/SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated). Today, tier is known at the edge (gateway) and in some control-plane surfaces, but it is not consistently propagated through routing/runtime, which makes per-tier SLI computation and burn-rate alerting unreliable.

This PR adds a single, low-cardinality tier dimension that is carried end-to-end with the request context and emitted consistently in metrics across gateway → routing → runtime.

What’s in this PR
- Defines canonical tier values: hosted | dedicated (and an internal-only unknown fallback for safety during rollout)
- Gateway: derives tier from request context (dedicated pool binding / customer config) and injects it into internal request metadata
- Routing: forwards tier through internal hops and attaches tier to routing metrics + traces
- Runtime: reads tier from request context and tags runtime request/latency/error metrics with tier
- Telemetry: updates metric definitions and label allowlists to ensure tier is recorded and does not explode cardinality
- Tests: unit tests for tier derivation + propagation; integration test that asserts tier label presence on a small set of core metrics

Notes / constraints
- Cardinality: tier is intentionally limited to two user-visible values. We explicitly prevent model/route/customer identifiers from being added as a side effect of this work.
- Backward compatibility: requests without tier metadata will be labeled tier="unknown" temporarily; follow-up will remove "unknown" once all ingress paths are updated.
- Dedicated correctness: tier is computed from the same binding used to route to dedicated capacity, so we should not see hosted traffic labeled as dedicated unless the binding is misconfigured.

Rollout plan
- Merge behind a default-on emission path but keep dashboards/alerts tolerant of tier="unknown" for ~1 week.
- After verifying in prod that unknown is near-zero, we’ll remove the fallback and enforce tier presence at ingress.

Related
- Pre-req for tiered SLI/SLO dashboards and error budget computation.
- Follow-up PR: update streaming disconnect classification to also include tier label in gateway metrics (tracked separately).

Screenshots / evidence
- Attached in internal thread: example Prometheus series now includes tier={"hosted"} and tier={"dedicated"} for gateway_request_total, routing_decision_total, runtime_tokens_total.

Checklist
- [x] Metrics label allowlist updated
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Reviewed with Telemetry for label hygiene
- [x] Rollout note added to internal runbook
commits: telemetry: add Tier enum + parsing helpers
gateway: derive tier from binding and inject into internal metadata
routing: forward tier through hop context; emit tier label on routing metrics
runtime: read tier from request ctx; tag latency/error/token metrics
tests: add propagation coverage + integration assertion on metric labels
docs: add tier label to metric catalog entries
conversation: Thomas Baird (review): Please confirm tier is hard-bounded. I’m worried about someone later passing through raw tenant tier strings and blowing cardinality. Can we enforce an allowlist at the parsing boundary and in the metric registry?

Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. Added Tier.ParseStrict() which only returns hosted/dedicated/unknown, and updated the metric label allowlist to explicitly enumerate allowed tier values. Also added a unit test that rejects arbitrary strings.

Nadia Rahman (review): For SLI correctness: make sure we don’t label client-side invalid auth / 4xx as dedicated just because the customer has a dedicated pool configured. Does tier derive from auth context or from successful binding?

Caleb Johnson (author): Tier is derived after tenant resolution (auth) but before binding. For requests that fail auth, we do not emit tier at all (gateway request rejected before context). For authorized requests, tier comes from the resolved tenant config + binding eligibility; if binding fails and we fall back to hosted, tier will be hosted. Added a comment in gateway middleware and a test for the bind-failure fallback.

Mina Haddad (review): Routing propagation looks good. One nit: in the router, you’re setting tier on the top-level context but not on the per-attempt context; retries might drop it. Can we attach to AttemptContext as well so per-attempt metrics also have tier?
Caleb Johnson (author): Fixed. Tier is now copied into AttemptContext and included in attempt-level metrics. Added regression test that simulates a retry and asserts tier label is preserved.

Amara Diallo (review): Gateway piece: can we ensure the header/metadata key name is consistent with our existing internal keys? Prefer x-ri-tier (or a structured metadata field) vs introducing a new key.
Caleb Johnson (author): Updated to use the existing internal metadata map key `ri.tier` (same namespace as `ri.route`), and removed the temporary header name. No change to external API headers.
Aisha Bello (review): +1 overall. Please add a short rollout note: dashboards should tolerate tier=unknown for a few days and alerts shouldn’t page on missing tier during rollout.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added rollout note to description and to docs/internal/metrics-catalog.md. Also updated integration test to allow unknown but assert presence of the label key.
Logan Wright (approval): Telemetry LGTM. Thanks for keeping tier bounded and adding allowlist enforcement.
release_notes: Internal only: metrics now include bounded `tier` label (hosted/dedicated) across gateway, routing, and runtime to support tiered SLO/error budget reporting.
